referencePatternsToCopy.label: Event detail and RSVP flow
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy an event detail layout: title, date/time, location, host, capacity/status chip, attendee context, RSVP action, and confirmation state.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the user’s current task.

findings.title: Workflow lifecycle UX is incomplete
findings.summary: 13 workflow/persona lifecycle scorecards failed. The UI is still proving action-card completion rather than full production workflow lifecycles.
findings.requiredFix: Use the failed lifecycle scorecards to add concrete objects, decision information, semantic primary and alternate actions, persistent result state, and receiver/continuation state before recapturing evidence.

findings.title: Primary experience still uses one repeated workflow-card renderer across unrelated communities
visibleEvidence: Workflow triptychs show the same top app bar, large colored hero card, pill status chips, bordered review card, and bottom primary button repeated across Garden Club, Book Club, Youth Soccer, HOA, Masjid, Chess, Camera, Platform Social, Ad-Free, and Data Portability rows.
Representative rows: b25-v4-row-002, b25-v4-row-050, b25-v4-row-065, b25-v4-row-113, and b25-v4-row-179 share the same structural template despite different user jobs.

The template is domain-labeled, but it does not create production-native surfaces such as a real feed, inbox/thread, payment receipt, facility calendar, review queue, export console, roster manager, or media critique surface.
findings.requiredFix: Replace the generic workflow-card renderer as the primary UX. Build domain-native surfaces per community/job: event detail and RSVP, donation/payment checkout and receipt, inbox/thread, facility calendar, approval queue, export wizard with real step navigation, roster table/detail, marketplace listing, and critique/media detail.
acceptanceCriteria: A fresh screenshot review can identify each primary workflow surface by domain structure before reading the workflow name.
Unrelated communities no longer share the same hero-card/status-chip/review-card/action-button skeleton as their primary screen.
Every primary workflow has a domain-native entry, action, result, and where applicable receiver/continuation state visible in screenshots.
findings.description: Primary experience still uses one repeated workflow-card renderer across unrelated communities

findings.title: User-facing copy still exposes review, evidence, platform, and harness language
visibleEvidence: 52 rows include the exact generic phrase "Review the object details, editable fields, final status, and continuation path before saving."
8 rows expose "Local package details" in the user-facing screen.
31 rows expose "Wizard progress" as the dominant surface, often without richer product context.
Rows b25-v4-row-185 and b25-v4-row-186 show a "Choose persona" dialog with "Preview the community experience for each member role," which is a testing harness surface.
Rows b25-v4-row-121 through b25-v4-row-123 expose "Top banner no-fill" and no-fill audit language to a member-facing surface.
findings.requiredFix: Rewrite screens in domain user language and remove evidence/test/framework copy. Move persona switching, local package details, no-fill diagnostics, workflow IDs, and generic review scaffolding out of production surfaces or behind explicit developer-only evidence tooling.
acceptanceCriteria: No reviewed screenshot contains "Local package details", "Review the object details", "Choose persona", "Preview the community experience", "Top banner no-fill", workflow IDs, or equivalent framework/test language.
Review/confirmation copy names the user object and decision, such as "Confirm Ramadan announcement", "Review dues payment", or "Resolve import conflicts", not generic object/status language.
findings.description: User-facing copy still exposes review, evidence, platform, and harness language

findings.title: Distinct workflow rows reuse identical screenshot pixels and do not prove distinct production states
visibleEvidence: 195 screenshot paths were verified, but only 181 screenshot hashes are unique.
Rows b25-v4-row-130/131/132 for export-import-replay are pixel-identical to rows b25-v4-row-175/176/177 for export-import-preview.
Rows b25-v4-row-133/134/135 for export-full-bundle are pixel-identical to rows b25-v4-row-157/158/159 for export-redacted-bundle.
Rows b25-v4-row-098 and b25-v4-row-101 reuse the same Chess Club home action screenshot for two different workflows.
Rows b25-v4-row-116 and b25-v4-row-143 reuse the same Member Social Space message action screenshot for two different workflows.
findings.requiredFix: Recapture or redesign distinct workflow states so each workflow/persona row proves its own object, action, result, and continuation state.
acceptanceCriteria: Different workflow IDs do not share identical PNG hashes for primary action/result proof unless explicitly accepted as the same user-visible state.
Export/import, redaction, checksum, transfer, rollback, and preview flows show different object details, controls, result states, and receipts.
The LLM freshness gate reports reviewed hashes matching the current run and duplicate groups are resolved or documented as intentionally shared non-primary states.
findings.description: Distinct workflow rows reuse identical screenshot pixels and do not prove distinct production states

findings.title: Workflow lifecycles are not visually complete enough for production handoff, receipt, and recovery states
visibleEvidence: The screenshot triptychs often change status text while retaining the same card shell instead of moving through a real form, review, success, receipt, receiver, or recovery surface.
Rows b25-v4-row-016 through b25-v4-row-018 show a soccer roster flow whose action/result is a card review rather than a roster manager with primary editing semantics.

Rows b25-v4-row-121 through b25-v4-row-123 and b25-v4-row-145 through b25-v4-row-147 show ad/no-fill and sensitive no-fill states as audit cards rather than production member-facing privacy/ad controls.

Rows b25-v4-row-136 through b25-v4-row-138, b25-v4-row-154 through b25-v4-row-156, and b25-v4-row-178 through b25-v4-row-183 show export steps without visually complete alternate, rollback, persistent result, or recovery affordances.
findings.requiredFix: For each failing lifecycle, add the missing production state: concrete object/context, decision information, primary semantic action, alternate/change/reject path, durable result/receipt, and receiver or continuation surface.
acceptanceCriteria: The 13 failing lifecycle scorecards rerun green with screenshot-visible proof for primary action, alternate/recovery path, persistent result, and receiver/continuation where required.

Completion screenshots show durable state such as receipt, notification delivery/read state, saved roster/standings, export artifact, rollback status, or inbox/feed continuation rather than only a status chip.
findings.description: Workflow lifecycles are not visually complete enough for production handoff, receipt, and recovery states

findings.title: Visual polish is below the production bar because of title truncation, dense card stacks, and one-note per-community palettes
visibleEvidence: Full-size row b25-v4-row-121 shows the app bar title clipped as "Member Social Spa..." beside two large shell icons.
The contact sheets show long community names repeatedly clipped in the top bar while the main content is dense with large text blocks and many status chips.
Most communities are dominated by one hue family per screen, with limited image/content variation and little visual identity beyond a generic icon in a circular badge.
Several screens use large stacked cards for every state, creating repeated-card fatigue and weak hierarchy across long review/result screens.
findings.requiredFix: Polish the shell and information hierarchy: avoid clipped primary titles, reduce chip density, use tabs/sections/lists/forms where appropriate, add community-specific identity/content treatment, and vary surface composition by task while preserving accessibility.
acceptanceCriteria: Primary app bar/community titles are not visibly clipped in reviewed screenshots, or the UI uses an intentional compact title/navigation pattern.
Long screens are broken into scannable sections with appropriate controls instead of repeating the same card/chip stack.
Visual identity and content hierarchy differ by community and workflow enough that a fresh reviewer does not classify the experience as a one-template scaffold.
findings.description: Visual polish is below the production bar because of title truncation, dense card stacks, and one-note per-community palettes

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does the whole UI feel like a modern production community product for the target personas, not merely implemented workflow screens?
visibleEvidence: All 195 PNGs were inspected via workflow triptychs; the same colored hero card, status chips, review card, and bottom action pattern repeats across unrelated communities and jobs.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Replace the generic workflow-card renderer as the primary UX. Build domain-native surfaces per community/job: event detail and RSVP, donation/payment checkout and receipt, inbox/thread, facility calendar, approval queue, export wizard with real step navigation, roster table/detail, marketplace listing, and critique/media detail.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Is the information architecture centered on real user jobs and community content?
visibleEvidence: Screens contain domain content such as events, dues, donations, care requests, and exports, but the IA is presented as uniform workflow cards rather than distinct feeds, inboxes, calendars, forms, receipts, and queues.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Promote community sections and job-native destinations over a uniform workflow card list/review model.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does the copy sound like product language rather than workflow/spec/test/evidence language?
visibleEvidence: 52 rows include the exact generic phrase "Review the object details, editable fields, final status, and continuation path before saving."
8 rows expose "Local package details" in the user-facing screen.
31 rows expose "Wizard progress" as the dominant surface, often without richer product context.
Rows b25-v4-row-185 and b25-v4-row-186 show a "Choose persona" dialog with "Preview the community experience for each member role," which is a testing harness surface.
Rows b25-v4-row-121 through b25-v4-row-123 expose "Top banner no-fill" and no-fill audit language to a member-facing surface.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Rewrite screens in domain user language and remove evidence/test/framework copy. Move persona switching, local package details, no-fill diagnostics, workflow IDs, and generic review scaffolding out of production surfaces or behind explicit developer-only evidence tooling.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Are visual hierarchy, spacing, typography, color, and component variety shippable?
visibleEvidence: Full-size row b25-v4-row-121 shows the app bar title clipped as "Member Social Spa..." beside two large shell icons.
The contact sheets show long community names repeatedly clipped in the top bar while the main content is dense with large text blocks and many status chips.
Most communities are dominated by one hue family per screen, with limited image/content variation and little visual identity beyond a generic icon in a circular badge.
Several screens use large stacked cards for every state, creating repeated-card fatigue and weak hierarchy across long review/result screens.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Polish the shell and information hierarchy: avoid clipped primary titles, reduce chip density, use tabs/sections/lists/forms where appropriate, add community-specific identity/content treatment, and vary surface composition by task while preserving accessibility.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Are title truncation, clipping/crowding, repeated-card fatigue, over-prominent platform banners, one-note palettes, and harness surfaces absent?
visibleEvidence: Full-size row b25-v4-row-121 shows "Member Social Spa..." truncation; rows b25-v4-row-185 and b25-v4-row-186 show a persona picker harness; repeated card stacks are visible in every workflow triptych sheet.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Resolve clipped shell titles, remove harness/persona picker surfaces from production review, and reduce repeated card density.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does each screen provide the concrete content and lifecycle actions a real user needs?
visibleEvidence: Many rows include concrete domain content, but 13 workflow/persona lifecycles lack screenshot-visible primary action, alternate path, persistent result, or semantic interaction proof.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: For each failing lifecycle, add the missing production state: concrete object/context, decision information, primary semantic action, alternate/change/reject path, durable result/receipt, and receiver or continuation surface.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Can B25 pass from this fresh screenshot-first review?
visibleEvidence: Unresolved counts: 1 blocker, 4 major, 0 minor. Any blocker or major finding blocks B25.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Resolve all blocker and major findings, recapture full B25 screenshots, rerun the LLM review/importer/lifecycle/production judges, and regenerate remediation tickets and iteration scorecard.

findings.title: Primary experience still uses one repeated workflow-card renderer across unrelated communities
visibleEvidence: Workflow triptychs show the same top app bar, large colored hero card, pill status chips, bordered review card, and bottom primary button repeated across Garden Club, Book Club, Youth Soccer, HOA, Masjid, Chess, Camera, Platform Social, Ad-Free, and Data Portability rows.
Representative rows: b25-v4-row-002, b25-v4-row-050, b25-v4-row-065, b25-v4-row-113, and b25-v4-row-179 share the same structural template despite different user jobs.

The template is domain-labeled, but it does not create production-native surfaces such as a real feed, inbox/thread, payment receipt, facility calendar, review queue, export console, roster manager, or media critique surface.
findings.requiredFix: Replace the generic workflow-card renderer as the primary UX. Build domain-native surfaces per community/job: event detail and RSVP, donation/payment checkout and receipt, inbox/thread, facility calendar, approval queue, export wizard with real step navigation, roster table/detail, marketplace listing, and critique/media detail.
acceptanceCriteria: A fresh screenshot review can identify each primary workflow surface by domain structure before reading the workflow name.
Unrelated communities no longer share the same hero-card/status-chip/review-card/action-button skeleton as their primary screen.
Every primary workflow has a domain-native entry, action, result, and where applicable receiver/continuation state visible in screenshots.
findings.description: Primary experience still uses one repeated workflow-card renderer across unrelated communities

findings.title: User-facing copy still exposes review, evidence, platform, and harness language
visibleEvidence: 52 rows include the exact generic phrase "Review the object details, editable fields, final status, and continuation path before saving."
8 rows expose "Local package details" in the user-facing screen.
31 rows expose "Wizard progress" as the dominant surface, often without richer product context.
Rows b25-v4-row-185 and b25-v4-row-186 show a "Choose persona" dialog with "Preview the community experience for each member role," which is a testing harness surface.
Rows b25-v4-row-121 through b25-v4-row-123 expose "Top banner no-fill" and no-fill audit language to a member-facing surface.
findings.requiredFix: Rewrite screens in domain user language and remove evidence/test/framework copy. Move persona switching, local package details, no-fill diagnostics, workflow IDs, and generic review scaffolding out of production surfaces or behind explicit developer-only evidence tooling.
acceptanceCriteria: No reviewed screenshot contains "Local package details", "Review the object details", "Choose persona", "Preview the community experience", "Top banner no-fill", workflow IDs, or equivalent framework/test language.
Review/confirmation copy names the user object and decision, such as "Confirm Ramadan announcement", "Review dues payment", or "Resolve import conflicts", not generic object/status language.
findings.description: User-facing copy still exposes review, evidence, platform, and harness language

findings.title: Distinct workflow rows reuse identical screenshot pixels and do not prove distinct production states
visibleEvidence: 195 screenshot paths were verified, but only 181 screenshot hashes are unique.
Rows b25-v4-row-130/131/132 for export-import-replay are pixel-identical to rows b25-v4-row-175/176/177 for export-import-preview.
Rows b25-v4-row-133/134/135 for export-full-bundle are pixel-identical to rows b25-v4-row-157/158/159 for export-redacted-bundle.
Rows b25-v4-row-098 and b25-v4-row-101 reuse the same Chess Club home action screenshot for two different workflows.
Rows b25-v4-row-116 and b25-v4-row-143 reuse the same Member Social Space message action screenshot for two different workflows.
findings.requiredFix: Recapture or redesign distinct workflow states so each workflow/persona row proves its own object, action, result, and continuation state.
acceptanceCriteria: Different workflow IDs do not share identical PNG hashes for primary action/result proof unless explicitly accepted as the same user-visible state.
Export/import, redaction, checksum, transfer, rollback, and preview flows show different object details, controls, result states, and receipts.
The LLM freshness gate reports reviewed hashes matching the current run and duplicate groups are resolved or documented as intentionally shared non-primary states.
findings.description: Distinct workflow rows reuse identical screenshot pixels and do not prove distinct production states

findings.title: Workflow lifecycles are not visually complete enough for production handoff, receipt, and recovery states
visibleEvidence: The screenshot triptychs often change status text while retaining the same card shell instead of moving through a real form, review, success, receipt, receiver, or recovery surface.
Rows b25-v4-row-016 through b25-v4-row-018 show a soccer roster flow whose action/result is a card review rather than a roster manager with primary editing semantics.

Rows b25-v4-row-121 through b25-v4-row-123 and b25-v4-row-145 through b25-v4-row-147 show ad/no-fill and sensitive no-fill states as audit cards rather than production member-facing privacy/ad controls.

Rows b25-v4-row-136 through b25-v4-row-138, b25-v4-row-154 through b25-v4-row-156, and b25-v4-row-178 through b25-v4-row-183 show export steps without visually complete alternate, rollback, persistent result, or recovery affordances.
findings.requiredFix: For each failing lifecycle, add the missing production state: concrete object/context, decision information, primary semantic action, alternate/change/reject path, durable result/receipt, and receiver or continuation surface.
acceptanceCriteria: The 13 failing lifecycle scorecards rerun green with screenshot-visible proof for primary action, alternate/recovery path, persistent result, and receiver/continuation where required.

Completion screenshots show durable state such as receipt, notification delivery/read state, saved roster/standings, export artifact, rollback status, or inbox/feed continuation rather than only a status chip.
findings.description: Workflow lifecycles are not visually complete enough for production handoff, receipt, and recovery states

findings.title: Visual polish is below the production bar because of title truncation, dense card stacks, and one-note per-community palettes
visibleEvidence: Full-size row b25-v4-row-121 shows the app bar title clipped as "Member Social Spa..." beside two large shell icons.
The contact sheets show long community names repeatedly clipped in the top bar while the main content is dense with large text blocks and many status chips.
Most communities are dominated by one hue family per screen, with limited image/content variation and little visual identity beyond a generic icon in a circular badge.
Several screens use large stacked cards for every state, creating repeated-card fatigue and weak hierarchy across long review/result screens.
findings.requiredFix: Polish the shell and information hierarchy: avoid clipped primary titles, reduce chip density, use tabs/sections/lists/forms where appropriate, add community-specific identity/content treatment, and vary surface composition by task while preserving accessibility.
acceptanceCriteria: Primary app bar/community titles are not visibly clipped in reviewed screenshots, or the UI uses an intentional compact title/navigation pattern.
Long screens are broken into scannable sections with appropriate controls instead of repeating the same card/chip stack.
Visual identity and content hierarchy differ by community and workflow enough that a fresh reviewer does not classify the experience as a one-template scaffold.
findings.description: Visual polish is below the production bar because of title truncation, dense card stacks, and one-note per-community palettes

deterministicScaffoldHolisticQuestionAns.requiredFix: Complete workflow/persona coverage, lifecycle scorecards, and remediate visual/layout failures before claiming production-grade UX.

deterministicScaffoldHolisticQuestionAns.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target persona?

deterministicScaffoldHolisticQuestionAns.requiredFix: Use screenshot-derived visible text, fix incomplete workflow lifecycles, and fix detected checklist, repeated-card, thin-content, or weak-identity visual blockers before rerunning the judge.

deterministicScaffoldHolisticQuestionAns.question: Is the overall information architecture organized around community content and real jobs-to-be-done instead of workflow lists or validation surfaces?
deterministicScaffoldHolisticQuestionAns.why: Failing workflow/persona lifecycle scorecards or visual blockers prevent a holistic community IA pass.
deterministicScaffoldHolisticQuestionAns.requiredFix: Replace incomplete workflow-card UX with lifecycle-complete domain-native community sections and rerun scorecards.

deterministicScaffoldHolisticQuestionAns.question: Does the visible UI avoid blocking or major overlap, clipping, crowding, default-scaffold, repeated-card, checklist-modal, and thin-content defects?

deterministicScaffoldHolisticQuestionAns.requiredFix: Complete screenshot-backed review rows, fix incomplete workflow lifecycles, and remediate any row-level layout/content defects.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material detail surface composition
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Build a domain detail page with primary content, metadata, status, and actions instead of a generic task card.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the user’s current task.
